A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical study. Their complete main texts, equations, references and appendices are readable, and corresponding results and proofs can be matched despite restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds, mathematical examples and proofs, including Appendix A, but no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. Section 5 adds discussion and Appendix B discusses prior work; neither reports original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The softmax and leverage-score model definitions, input constraints and repeated fixed-input testing constructions are retained. The new discussion introduces no algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. Additional application domains mentioned in v2 belong to the literature discussion.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. Newly cited optimization and hypothesis-testing methods are prior work, not experimentally evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an empirical evaluation protocol, data split, training budget or evaluation metric configuration.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness experiments or empirical supplementary analyses are introduced. The mathematical examples concerning indistinguishable parameters and low-probability rows in Sections 2–4 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated runs, seeds, error bars or significance tests. The analytical success-probability guarantees remain unchanged.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries occur in either version. The reported sample-complexity bounds, numerical constants and illustrative mathematical calculations are unchanged.

T1.justification: The results in Sections 3–4 and proofs in Appendix A retain their assumptions, bounds and arguments. Theorem 3.6 explicitly repeats the existing definition of nu; other edits concern notation and presentation.

C1.justification: The abstract, Theorems 1.1–1.2 and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning constrained binary testing of softmax and leverage-score models. No new bound or problem setting is claimed.

C2.justification: New Section 5 elaborates how Hellinger sensitivity could identify LLM 'ability regions' and characterizes leverage-score distributions as a more general, complex case. Existing identifiability caveats and open computational questions remain.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies implementation, hardware, hyperparameter or code/data-release information. The added discussion provides no new reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 substantially expands coverage of parameter-efficient tuning, computational and learning limitations, and machine-learning applications of testing and leverage scores. Appendix B extends the retained softmax survey to vision, generative models and other applications. Section 5 explicitly positions the contribution relative to classical testing, citing Pensia et al. (2023, 2024).

P1.justification: v2 adds a Discussion section and navigation paragraphs, moves the existing softmax-related-work subsection into Appendix B, places references before appendices and removes the contents page. Wording and author information change, while the core technical narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes an ICML-style document with two-column main text and references, running headers, an integrated opening page and single-column appendices. Typography, equation wrapping and page composition change throughout; neither version contains research figures or result tables.

improvement.justification: Section 5 makes the adaptation of classical testing to structured matrix models and its intended practical relevance more explicit, while expanded related work supplies broader context. These are modest explanatory gains. The mathematical results and proofs remain unchanged, including existing inconsistencies such as the SoftMax wording in leverage-score Theorem 4.4.
